topics.name: Two religions chosen from Buddhism, Christianity, Catholic Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism and Sikhism
The existence of God and revelation
Religion, human rights and social justice

connections.why: Each religion's teachings provide the beliefs applied to relationships and family ethics
Beliefs about creation and the sanctity of life come from the studied religions' teachings
Arguments about God build on the conceptions of God taught in each religion
Teachings on forgiveness and just war derive from each religion's core beliefs
Religious teachings on justice and forgiveness shape views on crime and punishment
Concepts of human dignity and equality flow from religious teachings
Beliefs about God as creator connect to debates on the origins and value of life
Both themes apply teachings on justice, forgiveness and the use of force
Punishment debates connect to wider questions of human rights and justice
Gender roles in families link to debates on equality and human rights
The value of life underpins arguments about justice and the rights of the vulnerable
